verdict.rationale: Bento documents natural-language alert rules that compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook, which covers the notification channels. It also tracks cost per run and tool failure rates. However, the evidence never explicitly shows alerting on cost spikes, error-rate thresholds, or eval-score drops; that is only implied by free-form English rules, and all sources are vendor marketing or FAQ claims. missing for 10: explicit documentation of alert conditions for error-rate thresholds, cost spikes, and eval-score drops; detailed alerting docs or setup guide for the Slack, PagerDuty, and email integrations; independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can set alerts on error rates, cost spikes, or eval-score drops and get notified in Slack, PagerDuty, or email

citations.quote: Alerts are defined in plain natural language... Rules compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook.
Write alerts in English. Bento groups fires into incidents and judges each one real or benign
you see cost per run, tool failure rates, drift over prompt versions, and regressions across deploys out of the box.
